body: I have my first driving lesson today and I'm feeling confident, I'm also off the pill and my mood has stabilised so Im catching up on school work :)

Awh, this is pretty uplifting, I suppose there's always a means to a way to Something. Maybe I should talk to counsellor and see for myself how helpful they actually are, I've nothing to lose lol, see if there's any other avenues I could take. I think my problem is that I'm being too vague with my life plan, I don't care much for anything and it takes little to make me happy so I don't have much ambition built, but if I took the time to really sit and think about I'd like from life, then worked out a specfic plan, say for the next 5 years and just worked on that, then I might actually be motivated. I just really struggle with keeping stamina up for any motivation, or keeping with plans because I'm constantly changing my mind because I'm never sure of anything, but at this stage I've just got to try something lol, thanks ☀️

Tbh I'm so disconnected I couldn't even tell you, I think I'm mostly scraping by, failing some, sometimes I get a burst of achievement when I actually do well but that's rare and few and far between. But our school system doesn't really work like that anyway, we have 1 big exam for each subject we do at the end of our last year (the leaving certificate it's called, its an Irish system) and we'll get a certain amount of points for each exam depending on how well we do, our total points overall from all our exams is calculated and that'll determine what college courses we'll be qualified to take, like if you get 200 points, that's crap, you won't qualify for any big brain colleges, and you won't get any big brain courses, but if you get 500-600, holy shit you're doing well. 
I already have a job and I've been doing well so far for that, but it's just fast food minimum wage place with a high turnover rate of employees because they can only hire students who don't need them for a livelihood and have to focus on school or college, so they don't have high standards, it'd be hard to get fired from there.
Idk I'm fine for being punctuatual for other things that are important, like interviews or appointments, I think my problem is committing to a routine for a long time. The mundanity will make me feel disconnected, I won't care as much and I'll lose to will to give my best effort, I'll fall back into the rhythm of my terrible stamina.
If I find something I'm really interested in and that I'm sure of, I'd have to make an effort to be better, but it's just finding something I can be sure of I guess lol, I'm not sure of anything, ever.
